//: The pages of the application. A page is its entry: pages.<page>.entry is an ES module (app_page_<page>.js) that imports what the page is made of; the browser loads the modules it imports, and theirs in turn, in dependency order. Nothing else lists them.

pages.<page>.lazy.<group>: modules that load on first use, through loader.loadGroup(group) (app_loader.js): the page names them here and imports none of them. A page that has no such group gets {} from loadGroup and keeps the path without it (no highlighter on the MCP page, no WebAssembly adapter that a page does not list).

tools/page_shells.py copies each page's description ({ name, entry, files, lazy }) into its shell as <script type="application/json" id="chdashModules"> and the shell adds the entry as a module script; tools/build_page_css.py builds the page stylesheets from the modules the page can run (its closure and its lazy groups); tools/stage_static.py gives every module a content hash in the build. After a change of an import or of this file, run python3 tools/build_page_css.py.

tools/module_graph.py (run by tools/build_page_css.py --check and the harness) fails on an import that is not a sibling module, on an import cycle, on a script that is on no page and on a lazy module that the page also imports.

app_common.js is what every entry imports first (the foundations and the components); app_boot.js is what every entry ends with. The pages: query (app_page_query.js); explorer, functions (the Explorer's Catalog and Functions: two pages of their own; the Functions page imports the Explorer controller and none of the graph, treemap, storage or table card modules, which the Catalog's entry hands over with explorer.use()); traces, logs, metrics (app_obs_page.js starts each view); trace (one trace: the trace view modules without the search page's parts); system, queries, disks (app_system.js starts each section); shape (one query shape); mcp (the access keys of the MCP endpoint, not tied to a host).
